headline: Approved prior meeting minutes 3-0; discussed city policy updates, supervisor training, and DPW open hours.
summary: Updates covered city policies, supervisor training, and open hours at the Department of Public Works. A Civilian Parking Enforcement Officer position is to be discussed at the request of the Pawtucket Police Department. The only recorded vote approved the minutes of the previous meeting, 3-0.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the July 6, 2026 meeting, 3-0.

transcript:
**Donald R. Grebien**
Mayor

# CITY OF PAWTUCKET

Pawtucket Municipal Annex
100 Freight Street, Room 204
PAWTUCKET, RHODE ISLAND 02860

## PERSONNEL BOARD MEETING

### Minutes

Tuesday August 11, 2026 - 6:00 P.M.

Meeting called to order at 6:00 PM.

1. Roll Call
   a. Present- Ken Riley, Joseph Shottek, Will Ruggiero
   b. Absent- Margaret Wingate, Patricia Martinez

2. Public Input Period – None

3. Approve and Accept Minutes of Previous Meeting
   a. Motion to amend July 6, 2026 minutes made by Joseph Shottek, 2nd by Will Ruggiero
      i. Amendment: change day in **Next Meeting** section from Monday, August 11, 2026 to "Tuesday, August 11, 2026".
      ii. Amendment: change location address in **Next Meeting** section from 75 Sabin Street Pawtucket, RI to "City Hall Annex, 100 Freight Street, Pawtucket, RI 02860, entrance at 75 Sabin Street."
   b. Motion to approve July 6, 2026 minutes made by Will Ruggiero, 2nd by Joseph Shottek. Approved 3-0

4. New Business
   a. City Policies: Update Status:
      i. Completed: as stated in April 13, 2026 Board meeting– FMLA policy, Dress Code policy and Racism in the Workplace have been updated.
      ii. Interview skills for hiring managers under consideration for future training.
      iii. Dress Down: Proceeds collected and beneficiary of donations: Dress Down policy generates approximately $150-$200 a month in donations and is higher during the Christmas holiday. Proceeds are donated to 6 or more non-profit Pawtucket charities or charities that serve Pawtucket residents. Charities include Pawtucket Soup Kitchen, Pawtucket Boys and Girls Club, Gloria Gemma Foundation, and Hero Package Foundation.
   c. Training -Supervisors:
      i. Completed: The City's Employee Assistance Program (EAP) provider recently delivered Customer Service training to Supervisors. Feedback suggested that the training was general and not tailored to a municipality environment.
      ii. Future Training: HR is seeking to provide future DEI training.
   d. HR Access
      i. Open Hours at DPW: time is set aside every other Thursday and these periods have proven impactful for connecting with DPW staff who do not have access to City e-mail. These periods have helped to address employee questions and resolve workplace issues early, including supervisor coaching and overtime scheduling issues.
   e. Future Business:
      i. Civilian Parking Enforcement Officer position to be discussed at the request of Pawtucket Police Department.

5. Old Business – None

6. Motion to Adjourn. Motion by Will Ruggiero, 2nd by Joseph Shottek. Approved 3-0.

The next meeting of the Board will be on Tuesday, September 1st, at 6:00 PM in Room 204 in the City Hall Annex, 100 Freight Street, Pawtucket, RI 02860, entrance at 75 Sabin Street.

The meeting adjourned at 7:03 PM.

Ken Riley, Chairman          Date
